observations.text: SP demonstrated formation airmanship at the level expected for this training unit, with the IP identifying No1's intentions and directing the timing of the wingman's actions throughout the sortie. Visual contact with the leader and awareness of the position of the other flight members were maintained once the IP established the references, and no briefed rule of formation flight was violated. Marginal performance for the Training Section - anticipation of No1's intention in advance, without assuming it, is expected to develop in the following sorties.

SP maintained visual contact with No1 and kept track of the position of the other flight members, with the IP's verbal prompts needed only for the anticipation of the leader's next maneuver. No part of the formation sortie had to be directed or executed by the IP, and the decision to reposition after the late rejoin was stated by SP with its rationale once prompted. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP put the wingman's tasks in sequence without dropping any of them, correlating the flight path of No1 with the assigned area and the fuel state throughout the sortie. Two late reactions to a change of the leader's power setting were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention, and the anticipated intention of No1 was confirmed by radio rather than assumed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP anticipated No1's intention in advance from the briefed profile and from the leader's flight path, and confirmed it rather than assuming it before each maneuver. Contingencies were identified, the decisions on the lost wingman procedure and on the fuel state were clearly stated with their rationale, and all wingman duties were carried out with minimum IP's supervision. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP correlated continuously what was happening in own A/C, in the formation and in the assigned area, and adjusted the execution of the mission to the remaining fuel and the prevailing weather without any prompting. No1's intention was anticipated in advance at every stage and confirmed before action was taken, with no assumption made at any point. Task loading was assessed before each phase, an alternative sequence was selected once in order to keep capacity in reserve, and every decision was clearly stated with its rationale. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a wingman's scan that dwelt on the leader's wing line to the exclusion of own A/C instruments and of the position of the other flight members, did not keep track of the formation's position relative to the assigned area boundary. The result was that the IP had to direct the recovery of orientation and execute part of the repositioning. Correlation of the formation flight path with the area limits before each maneuver is to be re-briefed.

SP, due to lack of awareness of the fuel state during the working phase of the sortie, did not assess the mission impact of the leader's request for an additional set-up and did not raise the bingo consideration with No1. The result was that the IP had to state the fuel condition to the flight and direct the recovery. Monitoring of the fuel state against the briefed bingo is to be re-briefed before the next formation sortie.

SP performed the wingman's duties at the level expected for this training unit, completing the position changes and the operational checks after the IP's verbal prompts. Deviations from the briefed formation position were recognized and corrected with delay, and No1's intention was read only after the leader's radio call rather than anticipated in advance. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier recognition of the cues given by the leader's flight path is expected to reduce the prompting required.

SP kept the wingman's tasks in sequence and monitored the Control and Performance Instruments of own A/C with reference to the leader and to the outside visual cues during maneuvering. Minor delays in matching the leader's power changes were recognized and corrected by SP in a timely manner without IP's intervention, and the anticipated intention of No1 was verified before it was acted upon. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP anticipated No1's intention in advance from the briefed profile and confirmed it before each maneuver, without assuming any part of it. The position of the other flight members, the fuel state and the area limits were tracked accurately throughout, decisions were clearly stated with their rationale, and all duties were carried out with minimum IP's supervision. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP correlated continuously the state of own A/C, the flight path of No1 and the position of the remaining flight members, and adjusted the execution of the mission to the remaining fuel and the prevailing weather without any prompting. Every anticipation of the leader's intention was confirmed before action, and no step of the briefed sequence was assumed. Task loading was assessed before each phase and an alternative course of action was selected once in order to keep capacity in reserve. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a lookout pattern that did not include the other flight members after the lead change, did not keep track of what was happening in the formation and did not identify the developing conflict with the second element. The result was that the IP had to direct the deconfliction and execute part of the repositioning. The clearing responsibilities of the wingman after a lead change are to be re-briefed.

SP, due to failure to exercise formation lead responsibilities after the lead change, did not put the tasks of the new role in order and did not state the intended maneuver to the wingman. The result was that the IP had to assume the lead of the formation and direct the remainder of the sequence. Further study of the flight lead duties described in the SOPs is required.

SP, due to a fuel and time check interval longer than the formation profile required, did not adjust the execution of the mission to the flight time remaining in the assigned area. The shortfall was identified only after the IP's verbal prompt, and the request to No1 for an early recovery was made with delay. The sortie was completed within the briefed limits, with the recovery flown as directed by the leader.

SP, due to lack of assertiveness in voicing a recognized unsafe condition, did not state to No1 that the briefed separation during the rejoin could not be maintained. The condition was called only after the IP's verbal prompt, with the result that the correction to the rejoin geometry was applied with delay. Use of the standard formation terminology to state a recognized hazard is to be re-briefed.

SP demonstrated formation airmanship within the desired standards, maintaining visual contact with No1, tracking the other flight members and correlating the fuel state with the limits of the assigned area. Two minor lapses in anticipating the leader's next maneuver were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention, but on both occasions the anticipation was reached later than the profile allowed. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier reading of No1's intention from the briefed profile is expected to improve.

SP anticipated No1's intention in advance at each stage of the profile and confirmed it before acting, without assuming any part of the leader's plan. Awareness of own A/C, of the other flight members and of the area limits was accurate throughout, decisions were clearly stated with their rationale, and all wingman duties were carried out with minimum IP's supervision. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP correlated continuously what was happening in own A/C, in the formation and in the assigned area, and adjusted the mission to the remaining fuel, the available flight time and the prevailing weather without any prompting. No1's intention was anticipated in advance throughout and verified before each action, with no assumption made at any point of the sortie. Capacity was managed deliberately, an alternative sequence being selected in order to keep task loading below the saturation point. Flight discipline was complete, with every required step carried out in the proper order. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a task sequence that placed the assessment of the rejoin geometry and the area boundary cross-check at the same point of the profile, did not maintain orientation relative to the assigned area during the rejoin. The result was that the IP had to direct the correction and execute part of the repositioning back inside the area. Separation of the rejoin assessment from the navigation cross-check is to be re-briefed.

SP, due to failure to make the knock-it-off call when the briefed parameters were exceeded, did not interrupt the maneuver after the briefed separation from No1 had been lost. The result was that the IP made the call and took the A/C in order to re-establish the separation. The knock-it-off criteria and the obligation of the wingman to call them are to be re-briefed before the next formation sortie.

SP, due to a cross-check that remained on the leader's wing line without returning to the fuel and engine indications of own A/C, did not track the fuel state during the working phase of the formation sortie. The bingo condition was recognized only after the IP's verbal prompt and the call to No1 was made with delay. The recovery was subsequently flown within the briefed limits.

SP, due to complacency in a familiar pattern that replaced an active scan, assumed No1's intention on the turn out of the area instead of anticipating it from the briefed profile and confirming it. The mismatch was recognized only after the IP's verbal prompt, with the result that the formation position was re-established late and outside the briefed geometry. Confirmation of the leader's intention before acting upon it is to be re-briefed.

SP, due to a power correction technique that lagged the leader's throttle changes during the turns, allowed the formation position to open beyond the briefed reference on two occasions. The deviation was identified by SP and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention, and the reference position was re-established before the following maneuver. Awareness of own A/C state, of the other flight members and of the area limits was otherwise maintained throughout the sortie.

SP, due to absent inquiry when the observed flight path of No1 did not match the briefed profile, acted on an anticipated intention that had not been confirmed with the leader. SP recognized the mismatch shortly afterwards, queried No1 on the intended maneuver and re-established the briefed position without IP's intervention. Task prioritization, orientation and the assessment of the other flight members were otherwise maintained for the remainder of the sortie.

SP demonstrated formation airmanship within the desired standards, maintaining awareness of own A/C, of No1 and of the other flight members, and carrying out all wingman duties with minimum IP's supervision. Anticipation of the leader's intention was correct but was reached late on two occasions, and the confirming radio call was made only when the maneuver had already begun. Marginal performance for the Training Section - speed in reading No1's intention in advance is expected to improve while the present accuracy of the awareness picture is maintained.

SP correlated continuously the state of own A/C, the flight path of No1 and the position of the remaining flight members, and adjusted the execution of the mission to the remaining fuel, the available flight time and the prevailing weather without any prompting. No1's intention was anticipated in advance at every stage and confirmed before action was taken, with no assumption made at any point. Task loading was assessed before each phase, an alternative sequence was selected in order to keep capacity in reserve, and every decision was clearly stated with its rationale. Flight discipline was complete, with all published rules and formation SOPs applied and every required step carried out in the proper order. Above end of block MIF achieved.
